name: Great Power
momentumNotes: Power is high and active; the danger is not weakness but excess without right conduct.
theme: Great Power is force in motion. Its test is whether strength can remain aligned with what is right.
basicInterpretation: You may have more power than usual now. Let conduct govern momentum, so that force becomes service rather than excess.
reflectionPrompt: How can your strength stay answerable to wisdom?

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Great Power becomes Hexagram 33, Retreat. This other side brings in the atmosphere of withdrawal, timing, distance, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let Retreat widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through Retreat. Notice where withdrawal, timing, distance and a withdrawing, declining movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Great Power is Hexagram 20, Contemplation. Where the primary pattern emphasizes strength, momentum, responsibility, this complementary field points toward observation, perspective, reverence.
opposite.reflection: This is not the main movement of the reading, but it shows what balances or challenges it. It can also highlight hidden causes or contrasting forces at play. Notice where Contemplation names the medicine, shadow, or unchosen path beside the situation.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize Contemplation as the contrasting color laid beside Great Power. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by observation, perspective, reverence, especially where the situation carries a contemplative, restrained tone.
